metaTitle: Best Our Place Air Fryers in 2026
metaDescription: Three Our Place Wonder Oven air fryer toaster ovens compared on 13 and 30 quart capacity, racks, steam infusion, touchscreen controls and cleanup.
expertTake: The Wonder Oven Pro 30 qt is the best of the three because its touchscreen, eight functions and steam infusion cover baking and everyday cooking in one oven. The 13 qt Wonder Oven is the pick for small kitchens. Skip the brand if you want a basket-style air fryer, since every model here is an oven.
introParagraphs: A design-led kitchenware brand can enter the air fryer market with a small range, and this one is built entirely around countertop ovens with an air fry mode. That makes the choice simpler than a broad catalogue but less flexible than a brand that sells baskets as well. A narrow range also means fewer reviews and fewer owner write-ups to lean on, so spec sheets and layout details carry more weight than usual.

Everything in a lineup like this is an oven with racks, a door and a fan, so the questions that matter are capacity, number of racks, control style and whether the extras justify the price over a plain air fryer toaster oven.

products.description:
The Wonder Oven Pro is a 30 quart oven with three racks, a digital touchscreen and eight functions that include proof and dehydrate. Built-in steam infusion is the standout, and the listing describes premium quartz and stainless steel heating elements that reach 450F.

Steam in a countertop oven is a real engineering step. It helps bread rise, keeps reheated food from drying out and gives pastries a better crust. The listing claims cooking up to 40 percent faster than a conventional oven. Compared with the 13 quart Wonder Oven, you get far more room and the steam system, and you pay for both in size and price.

Expect to dry the cavity after steam cooks to prevent water spots and to use filtered water in hard-water areas. The touchscreen wipes clean, though wet hands cause misreads. Plan for a large counter footprint and clearance on every side. Treat the faster-cooking claim as a comparison against an unspecified full-size oven, and expect real savings mostly from the short preheat. For bread, load the dough on the middle rack and run the proof setting first, then switch to bake so the steam does its work early in the cycle.
products.bestFor: Families who bake, reheat and cook for four or more.

products.description:
The Large Wonder Oven keeps the 30 quart, three-rack interior and drops to six functions: air fry, bake, roast, toast, broil and reheat. The product page says it fits sheet-pan dinners and multilevel cooking.

It is the simpler sibling of the Pro, without steam infusion, proof or dehydrate, and the listing does not mention a touchscreen. For a family that wants room for full meals rather than bakery tricks, that trade is reasonable. Against the 13 quart model, it offers more than twice the capacity and a third rack.

Expect to rotate trays for even browning, since racks nearer the fan cook faster. Wipe the interior and crumb tray regularly. Allow generous clearance for the door swing and the heat. Use the top and bottom racks for two trays at once and swap them halfway, since the upper level browns faster than the lower. A single full sheet pan on the middle rack gives the most even result. If you often cook for guests, the third rack is the reason to choose this size, because it lets you stage a main, a side and a tray of vegetables without batching.
products.bestFor: Families who want a big, simple oven without steam.
cons: Large and heavy for a counter

products.description:
The original Wonder Oven is a compact 13 quart oven with a 12 liter interior, two cooking levels and six functions. The listing quotes a dynamic 200F to 450F range and a preheat that is much faster than a traditional oven.

It handles meals for two to four people, which makes it the right size for a small kitchen that cannot spare the space for a 30 quart. Compared with the larger models, you give up rack count and capacity, and you gain a much smaller footprint and a quicker preheat.

A compact interior heats fast but restricts tray size, so measure the pans you intend to use. Wipe the crumb tray and cavity after each use. Leave clearance on all sides. A small oven is easy to place but unforgiving of large dishes, so measure your most-used baking tray before you order. Because the interior is only about twelve litres, preheat is short and the machine behaves like a roomy toaster oven. Many owners keep it on the counter for toast and reheating and bring out a larger oven only for big roasts.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens that need an oven for two to four people.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Every Our Place air fryer is a countertop oven with racks and a door, not a drawer. That suits bread, sheet pans and toast, and it handles air frying through a basket or tray with a strong fan. It does not replace a basket for a handful of fries, because the cavity is larger and slower to heat. The airflow also behaves differently: a basket forces air through the food from every side, while an oven moves air across a tray. Spread food in a single layer on a perforated pan, and turn it halfway for the closest match to basket results. If crisp frozen food is your main use, a dedicated basket remains the faster tool.

The Wonder Oven at 13 quarts fits meals for two to four in a small kitchen. The Large Wonder Oven and the Pro at 30 quarts add a third rack and room for sheet pans. Measure your counter and your pans before choosing, since the 30 quart models are big. A useful test is to place a full sheet pan next to the interior dimensions and check that it slides in with room for airflow on each side. Remember that a bigger cavity also takes longer to heat and uses more energy for a small dinner, so the larger oven is only a better choice if you will use the space.

The Wonder Oven Pro adds built-in steam. It helps bread rise, keeps reheated food moist and improves pastry crust. It also adds a water reservoir, drying and descaling chores. Decide whether you bake enough to use it. Steam helps most with crusty bread, bagels and reheated pizza, where moisture early in the cycle makes a visible difference. It does little for roasted vegetables or frozen snacks, which want dry heat. If most of your cooking is dry-heat, the plain 30 quart oven gives the same room for less upkeep.

The Pro has a digital touchscreen for precise time and temperature. The simpler models rely on basic controls. A touchscreen looks clean but can misread wet fingers, while simple controls are easy to read at a glance. Either way, check that the display is legible from a standing position and that the beep is audible across the room. Controls that you can operate with oven mitts on are a real advantage when you are pulling a hot tray.

The brand markets a non-toxic design, which we treat as a manufacturer claim. Oven cavities collect splatter and need wiping, and a crumb tray needs emptying. Steam models need drying after use. A damp cloth with a drop of mild soap handles most splatter once the oven has cooled, and a non-scratch pad deals with baked-on spots. Avoid harsh oven cleaners, which can damage coatings and leave residues that heat will vaporise. Pull the racks and wash them by hand every few weeks.

A large oven with fast elements draws heavily from a household circuit. The Pro lists quartz and stainless heating elements that reach 450F. Use a wall outlet and avoid sharing the circuit with a kettle or microwave. If your kitchen circuits are old, ask which outlets share a breaker, since a trip during a long bake is irritating and can spoil the dish. A dedicated spot near a heavy-duty outlet saves any temptation to use an extension cord.

howWeEvaluated.title: Whole lineup coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We covered every distinct Our Place air fry oven with a listing we could read. That meant three machines. We did not pad the list with other brands.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and racks
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared interior size and rack count. The 13 qt has two racks and the 30 qt models have three. Capacity decides which meals fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features and control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at steam, proof and the control interface. The Pro adds steam and a touchscreen, and the others keep it simpler. Extras matter only if used.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleanup and care
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted crumb trays, steam upkeep and interior wiping. Steam models need drying. The non-toxic marketing is the maker's claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed capacity and extras against where each oven sits in the range. The 13 qt is the smallest and the Pro is the largest. Listing prices change, so we judged value by tier without quoting a number. We also looked at how the three differ in what they ask of the owner, since steam, racks and a touchscreen each add a learning step. Because the range is small, we also noted overlaps: the Pro and the Large Wonder Oven share a 30 quart, three-rack body, so the real question is whether steam, proof and a touchscreen are worth the step up. We gave weight to what each listing actually states, and we avoided treating marketing speed claims as measured results.

howToChoose.note: Choose 13 quarts for space and 30 quarts for family cooking. In between sits the question of how often you cook for more than four people. If that is a few times a year, a 13 quart oven plus a regular oven for holidays is a sensible pair. If it is every week, the larger body will earn its counter spot.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for the size that matches your counter and your pans, and decide whether steam is worth the upkeep. Remember that every model here is an oven. Check the depth and height with the door open, confirm that your outlet is close enough to avoid an extension cord and make sure a cabinet above will not trap steam or heat.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Wonder Oven Pro is the best overall. The Large Wonder Oven suits a simple family oven, and the 13 qt suits a small kitchen.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You bake and want steam, proof and a touchscreen, which point to the Pro. A larger family also benefits from 30 quarts. The extra spend is easiest to justify for people who use the oven daily, since a machine that replaces both a toaster oven and a second small oven starts to pay back in counter space and convenience.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cook for two to four. The 13 qt Wonder Oven covers that at the lowest tier.

maintenance.why: Crumbs scorch and smoke on the next heat. Slide the tray out and tip it into a bin. A tray that is allowed to fill with crumbs and grease is the most common cause of smoke and odours in any toaster-style oven. Let it cool first, then wash it with warm soapy water.
Splatter bakes on the walls and elements. Wipe with the oven cool.

Standing water leaves spots and can cause odours. Leave the door open to air dry. Wipe the door glass as well, since steam leaves a film that is easy to remove while fresh and harder once baked on. A microfibre cloth leaves the fewest streaks.

Minerals build up in the steam path. Filtered water slows it. A white film or slower steam output are the signs it is time to descale, and the maker's manual describes the method that is safe for your model. Never use harsh chemicals in the steam path.

maintenance.task: Inspect the door seal and cord
maintenance.why: A poor seal loses heat and a worn cord is a hazard. Replace damaged parts. A door that no longer closes squarely is the most common early sign of trouble in any countertop oven. Check it with a sheet of paper in the seam. If the paper slides out freely when the door is shut, the seal is no longer doing its job and heat is escaping.

faq.q: Are Our Place air fryers really air fryers?
faq.a: They are countertop ovens with an air fry mode and a strong fan. They crisp well on perforated trays but heat more slowly than a basket. They also toast and bake.

faq.q: Which Our Place oven is best?
faq.a: The Wonder Oven Pro 30 qt is the best overall because of steam, proof and the touchscreen. The 13 qt suits small kitchens, and the Large Wonder Oven is the simple family option.
It helps bread, pastries and reheated food if you use it often. It adds water and descaling chores. Skip it if you rarely bake.

It is a manufacturer claim that we cannot confirm from a spec sheet. Read the product page for what is specifically stated about materials, such as which surfaces touch food and which coatings are used. Treat the phrase as a starting point for your own questions, not an answer, and check the care guide for how the interior should be cleaned.

faq.q: Can I replace my toaster oven?
faq.a: Yes, all three toast, bake and broil. The 30 quart models also take sheet pans. Check your pan sizes against the interior. A quarter-sheet pan fits most countertop ovens, while a half-sheet needs the 30 quart models. Also check the tallest item you roast, since a chicken or a deep casserole may touch the top element in a smaller cavity.

The listings advertise preheats far shorter than a full-size oven, and a compact cavity does warm quickly. Treat the exact percentages as marketing claims. In daily use, expect a few minutes to reach cooking temperature, longer for the 30 quart models.
